marked.s: If Someone Says "My Brain Feels Damaged": DMSO + Humic Acid + Electrolytes First
Smelling humic acid or tasting a tiny bit can also help a lot, in my experience, but I'm still collecting data from others.
I add electrolytes too, because magnesium (and then potassium) can be depleted by some drugs, especially MDMA and iboga, although I don't think just electrolytes would be sufficient.
- First, are they unconscious or breathing abnormally?
- Feel whether they're very hot.
- Ask about a really bad headache or chest pain.
- Check if their vision has changed.
When they're too out of it to help you do the checks, or if the brain-damage feeling stays despite sufficient treatment, then you've done what you can do, and it's time to call for help.

marked.s: In an emergency room, a scared, psychotic-feeling person will often get a benzodiazepine.
Those only sometimes help with psychosis, and in some people they bring on more agitation or fear instead, a paradoxical reaction.
Antipsychotics may work better for psychosis, but they carry their own risks and interactions, and the staff giving them often don't know what was taken, if anything.
Even from a severe trip, they can come down faster that way than after an ambulance ride and hours in an emergency room.
Don't count on it helping with psychosis, since in some people it does the opposite and brings on more agitation or fear, which is called a paradoxical reaction.
